sourcing: This is our own practice test. It is not an official exam, and no text in it comes from an exam paper. The task types (short conversations, announcements, telephone messages, short texts, adverts, signs, a form and a short message) are modelled loosely on the task types of Cambridge A2 Key, but the language is kept at A1 level. Every task was written by EnglishAcademy.
passNote: The 60 % pass line is our own convention. It is not an official pass mark, because there is no official exam behind this test. Only Listening and Reading (30 tasks) are marked automatically. You compare the Writing tasks yourself, and Speaking needs another person, so neither is counted.

teil1.instruction: You hear each text twice. Choose a, b or c.

items.prompt: What time is the second train to Leeds?
items.transcript: “Excuse me. When is the next train to Leeds?” — “At ten past nine.” — “Thank you. And the next one after that?” — “At twenty to ten.”

items.prompt: What does the man buy?
items.transcript: “Hello. Two apples, please.” — “I’m sorry, we have no apples today. We have pears and bananas.” — “OK. Two bananas, please.”

items.prompt: Where does Mrs Costa work now?
items.transcript: “Do you still work in the shop, Mrs Costa?” — “No. I work in a school now. My husband works in the shop.”

items.prompt: What is the weather on Saturday?
items.transcript: “Here is the weather for the weekend. On Saturday it is cold and it snows all day. On Sunday it is sunny.”

items.prompt: How much is the ticket?
items.transcript: “One ticket to Bath, please.” — “Single or return?” — “Return, please.” — “That is fifteen pounds.”

items.prompt: What must Ben buy?
items.transcript: “Hi Ben, it’s Mum. We have bread and milk. Please buy some eggs. Thanks!”

teil2.instruction: You hear four announcements. You hear each announcement once. Are the sentences true or false?

items.prompt: The train to Bristol leaves from platform 6.
items.transcript: “Attention, please. The train to Bristol now leaves from platform 6, not from platform 2. We are sorry.”

items.prompt: The shop closes in one hour.
items.transcript: “Dear customers, the shop closes in ten minutes. Please go to the till now. Thank you.”

items.prompt: The English class is later today.
items.transcript: “This is for students in English class A1. The class starts at ten o’clock today, not at nine o’clock. The room is the same.”

items.prompt: The surgery is open on Friday afternoon.
items.transcript: “Welcome to the doctor’s surgery. We are open from Monday to Thursday, from eight o’clock to six o’clock. On Friday we are open from eight o’clock to twelve o’clock.”

teil3.instruction: You hear five telephone messages. You hear each message twice. Choose a, b or c.

items.prompt: Where do the two people meet?
items.transcript: “Hi Priya, it’s Tom. The café is closed today. Please come to the cinema. See you later!”

items.prompt: When is Mrs Khan’s appointment now?
items.transcript: “Hello, Mrs Khan. This is the doctor’s surgery. Your appointment on Tuesday is not possible. Can you come on Thursday at three o’clock? Please call me back.”

items.prompt: What is the problem?
items.transcript: “Hello, Mr Novak. This is Mrs Green from next door. There is water in your kitchen. Please call me now. My number is 07700 900 456.”
options: There is water in the kitchen.
items.answer: There is water in the kitchen.

items.prompt: What must the customer do?
items.transcript: “Hello, this is the post office. Your parcel is here. Please come to the post office before Saturday. Bring your passport.”

items.prompt: You are a student. How much is the English course?
items.transcript: “Hello, this is Park College. The English course is 120 pounds. For students it is 80 pounds. Please sign up before 30 September.”

teil1.instruction: Read the two texts. Are sentences 1–5 true or false?

texts.label: Text 1 — Email
texts.body:
Dear Amina,

How are you? I am in Manchester now. I live in a small room. It is nice and not expensive: £350 a month. My English class starts on Monday. It is every day from 9 to 12. In the afternoon I work in a café.

Can you come in the summer? We can go to the lake.

Love
Yusuf

texts.label: Text 2 — Text message
texts.body: Hi Max, I am still at the office. The meeting is long. Can you get the children from school? I am home at 6 o’clock. There is soup in the fridge. Thanks! Lena

items.prompt: Yusuf lives in Manchester.
His room is £350 a week.
Yusuf works in a café in the morning.
Lena is home at 6 o’clock.
The meeting is short.

teil2.instruction: Read situations 6–10 and adverts a and b. Which advert is right? Choose a or b.

items.situation: You want an English class in the evening. You work in the day.

options.label: Lingua School — English classes A1–B2, Monday to Friday, 9 to 12. Small groups.
Evening College — English in the evening, Tuesday and Thursday, 6 to 8.30 pm. Good for people with jobs.
Market Pharmacy — Monday to Friday 8 am to 6.30 pm, Saturday 9 am to 1 pm. Closed on Sunday.
Late Pharmacy — open every Sunday, 9 am to 8 pm.

items.situation: You want a flat for you and your dog.

options.label: 2-room flat with a balcony, £690 a month. Dogs and cats are OK.
2-room flat, quiet, £640 a month. No dogs or cats. No smoking.

items.situation: Your bike is broken. You want it ready today.

options.label: Meyer Bikes — we mend your bike in one day. Bring it before 10 am. Take it home in the evening.
The Bike Shop on Park Road — we sell new and old bikes. We do not mend bikes.

items.situation: You need someone for your children on Saturday evening.

options.label: Sunshine Nursery — Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm. Children from 1 year. Ask at the office.
Student (22) looks after children at the weekend. Evenings are OK. Phone 07700 900 321.

teil1.instruction: Your friend Maria Sanchez wants to join an English class. You help her with the form. Write the five missing answers.
teil1.context: Maria Sanchez was born on 4 July 1996 in Seville. She is Spanish. She lives at 12 Lime Street, Leeds LS1 4AB. She is a nurse and works in a hospital. She wants the A1 class in the evening.

teil2.instruction: Write a short message (about 30 words). Answer all three points.
teil2.task: Your English class starts tomorrow, but you are ill. Write an email to your teacher, Mrs Berger.
points: Say when you will come again.
teil2.model:
Dear Mrs Berger,

I cannot come to class tomorrow. I am ill and I have a cold. Can you tell me the homework, please? I will come again on Monday.

Best wishes
Amina Yilmaz
checklist: There is a greeting and an ending (Dear … / Best wishes).
All three points are in your message.
